jobs.title: Tech Principal Product Manager
jobs.description:
About the Team
You will be a key member of the Supply Chain Product Management team responsible for delivering technology capabilities that modernize and optimize Williams-Sonoma's end-to-end supply chain. The team partners closely with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Merchandising, Engineering, Architecture, Analytics, and Technology to deliver scalable product capabilities that improve operational efficiency, inventory productivity, manufacturing performance, and customer experience. You will be a key member of the Supply Chain Product Management team that is responsible for continuous improvement of our supply chain by focusing on removing friction points for our internal and external customers by delivering a highly satisfying experience.

About the Role:
Williams-Sonoma, Inc. is in the business of enhancing the quality of our customers' lives at home.  This critical Principal Product Manager role owns the product strategy, roadmap, and execution for Williams-Sonoma's Manufacturing technology domain, supporting our in-house furniture and lighting manufacturing operations. This leader will define and deliver capabilities that improve manufacturing planning, production execution, inventory visibility, quality, scheduling, materials management, shop floor operations, and fulfillment while enabling scalable growth across our manufacturing network.  This role operates across strategy and execution, partnering with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Technology leaders to define product strategy, prioritize investments, and deliver measurable business outcomes across Williams-Sonoma's manufacturing network. The right candidate will have deep experience with discrete manufacturing as well as the associated logistics and transportation activities and a techno-functional / Product Management background.

Responsibilities
- This role operates across product strategy and execution, partnering with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Technology leaders to modernize manufacturing capabilities and deliver measurable business outcomes across Williams-Sonoma's manufacturing network.
- Own the Manufacturing product strategy, roadmap, and investment priorities, identifying opportunities through customer insights, operational data, and hypothesis-driven product discovery focused on measurable business outcomes.
- Monitor emerging manufacturing, supply chain, ERP, AI, and digital manufacturing trends, evaluating new technologies and industry practices that can improve Williams-Sonoma's competitive advantage.
- Define product success metrics and measurement plans tied to manufacturing efficiency, production throughput, inventory accuracy, schedule adherence, quality, operational productivity, adoption, and business value realization. Continuously measure outcomes to guide product investment decisions and optimization.
- Lead product discovery, business process analysis, and solution definition for manufacturing capabilities, translating business needs into product strategy, roadmaps, epics, features, user stories, acceptance criteria, and prioritized Jira backlogs that enable iterative Agile delivery.
- Identify, prioritize, and deliver AI-enabled capabilities that improve manufacturing planning, shop floor productivity, quality, scheduling, operational efficiency, and business decision making while leveraging generative AI to improve product discovery, requirements quality, documentation, and team productivity.
- Serve as the primary product leader across Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Engineering, Architecture, and Technology teams, aligning stakeholders around product vision, priorities, delivery, and measurable business value.
- Partner with Engineering and Architecture teams to deliver iterative product capabilities using Agile methodologies while balancing business value, technical debt, scalability, and long-term platform health.
- Serve as the manufacturing product subject matter expert, leading cross-functional exploration, making informed product recommendations, and communicating roadmap priorities, tradeoffs, progress, and outcomes to business partners and senior Technology leadership.
- Lead organizational readiness and product adoption activities, including stakeholder alignment, business process design, SOP documentation, training, UAT, hyper-care, and adoption measurement.
- Ensure manufacturing solutions meet governance, security, audit, licensing, and compliance requirements while partnering with Internal Audit and Technology teams to establish appropriate operational controls.

Criteria

- 10 years of Product Management or techno-functional experience supporting Manufacturing, Supply Chain, ERP, or related enterprise technology platforms.

- Experience with discrete manufacturing, configurable products, production planning, bills of material, routings, work centers, capacity planning, quality management, and manufacturing execution preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to influence senior business and technology leaders, drive executive alignment, manage competing priorities, and communicate effectively across executive, operational, and technical audiences without direct authority.
- Deep understanding of Microsoft Dynamics AX/Dynamics 365 Manufacturing, Supply Chain Management, Production Control, Inventory Management, Procurement, Warehouse Management, and related manufacturing processes.
- Demonstrated experience owning product strategy, roadmaps, and execution for complex enterprise platforms supporting manufacturing or supply chain operations.
- Own the product lifecycle from discovery through adoption, continuously measuring business outcomes and incorporating customer feedback into future roadmap priorities.
- Experience applying AI, generative AI, machine learning, automation, or advanced analytics to improve manufacturing operations, product management practices, or business processes. Demonstrated ability to identify and deliver AI-enabled business capabilities.
- Experience with related supply chain operations, order management, eCommerce and finance / accounting processes.
- Experience leading large-scale business transformation initiatives from product discovery through implementation, including business process redesign, organizational change management, UAT, training, and production adoption.
- Experience with the process of configurable products as they flow from the eCommerce customer’s orders through order management (OMS) and to Dynamics 365 for manufacturing and order fulfillment.
- You have a proven ability to understand and discuss technical concepts, manage difficult tradeoffs, and evaluate new ideas with partners across the organization.
- Experience in a large, multi-brand business preferred. Consulting experience is also desirable.
- Experience creating and managing product backlogs, including writing epics, features, user stories, acceptance criteria, and prioritizing work within Jira for Agile software delivery.
- Strong communication and negotiation skills and the ability to lead and influence others.
- Bachelor's degree or more in Engineering, Marketing, Computer Science, or a related field or equivalent work experience.
- This role requires being onsite in the WSI manufacturing Claremont, North Carolina office Monday through Thursday.
- Some travel will be required to other WSI manufacturing and supply chain locations within the United States. (Manufacturing: Claremont, NC; Tupelo, MS; Portland, OR)

Our Culture & Values
We believe that taking care of our people is vital to our success and we strive to offer equitable and transparent practices for all. We prioritize connection, growth, and wellbeing.
People First
Putting People First means investing in overall well-being and opportunities to grow and advance within the organization. Depending on the position and location, here are a few highlights of what benefits may be available:

Benefits
- A generous discount on all WSI brands

- A 401(k) plan and other investment opportunities

- Paid vacations, holidays, and time off to volunteer

- Health benefits, dental and vision insurance, including same-sex domestic partner benefits

- Tax-free commuter benefits

- A wellness program that supports your physical, financial and emotional health

Continued Learning
- In-person and online learning opportunities through WSI University

- Cross-brand and cross-function career opportunities

- Resources for self-development

- Advisor (Mentor) program

- Career development workshops, learning programs, and speaker series

This role is not eligible for relocation assistance.
Williams-Sonoma, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Williams-Sonoma, Inc. will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, or other applicable state or local laws and ordinances.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Web Merchandising
jobs.description:
About Williams-Sonoma India Technology Center
Williams-Sonoma India Technology Center is the technology hub for Williams-Sonoma, Inc., supporting global digital commerce, supply chain, enterprise platforms, and customer experiences across our portfolio of brands. The India Technology Center partners closely with global business and engineering teams to build scalable, resilient, and innovative platforms that serve millions of customers worldwide.
About the Team
The Merchandising Systems Product Management team is responsible for the technology platforms and tools that support the end-to-end product lifecycle across Williams-Sonoma, Inc. brands, from initial item intake and item setup through product enrichment, merchandising, and publication across all channels.
Our ecosystem includes Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), Product Information Management (PIM), Digital Asset Management (DAM), Web Assortment Management (WAM), and downstream eCommerce systems. Together, these capabilities enable our brands to manage product information, content, and assets efficiently at scale for our customers.
By improving these technology solutions, we help WSI bring new product assortments to market faster, improve product and content quality, reduce manual effort, and respond effectively to evolving product, market, and customer needs.
About the Role
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to join the Merchandising Systems team at our India Technology Center in Pune.
Web merchandising is at the heart of WSI's eCommerce business, shaping how millions of products are brought to life across our brands and digital experiences. Your initial focus will be Web Assortment Management (WAM), a major multi-year transformation replacing a legacy platform that has supported the business for more than 16 years. WAM will become the core platform for organizing, enriching, validating, reviewing, and publishing online assortments across WSI's eCommerce sites.
In this hands-on role, you will translate product strategy into well-defined capabilities and drive them through delivery and brand adoption. You will work closely with the Engineering team in Pune and partner with US-based Product, business, UX, Architecture, and Technology teams. A US-based Lead Product Manager will set overall WAM direction and priorities; within that direction, you will define requirements, make product decisions, manage dependencies, and drive assigned capabilities from concept through rollout.
A significant part of the role is helping brand users successfully adopt new WAM capabilities and processes. You will study current workflows, identify improvement opportunities, demonstrate new functionality, develop and deliver training, support User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and guide users through the transition from legacy tools and processes.
WAM will be the primary focus as the platform is delivered, launched, and scaled. Over time, the role may expand to other enterprise merchandising and content platforms, including Digital Asset Management and Site Content Management.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will...
- Own product execution for assigned WAM capabilities and workstreams, translating product strategy and priorities into detailed requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and delivery plans.
- Partner closely with the Pune Engineering team throughout the product development lifecycle, providing product context, resolving requirements questions, making trade-offs, and ensuring delivered solutions achieve intended business outcomes.
- Develop deep expertise in WAM, online assortment management, and the workflows used by brand teams to manage product assortment and content at scale.
- Partner with brand users and US-based Product and business stakeholders to understand current processes, pain points, workarounds, and requirements, and translate them into scalable solutions across WSI brands.
- Partner with UX to translate complex business workflows into intuitive experiences for business users.
- Work with Engineering and Architecture on platform capabilities, data models, integrations, validation and publishing workflows, and dependencies across PIM, DAM, image services, and eCommerce systems.
- Translate abstract technical concepts and complex system behavior into clear product requirements, practical workflows, and solutions that business users can understand.
- Identify risks, requirements gaps, edge cases, and cross-system dependencies early, and maintain a clear, actionable backlog that provides Engineering with the context needed for delivery.
- Lead or support UAT, including scenario definition, business-user coordination, issue triage, and translation of findings into product improvements.
- Drive business readiness and adoption through stakeholder engagement, workflow documentation, product demonstrations, training and enablement, rollout support, and ongoing feedback.
- Measure product effectiveness using qualitative and quantitative feedback, including adoption, workflow efficiency, time to market, data quality, platform performance, and business-user satisfaction.
- Identify opportunities to simplify workflows, reduce manual effort, improve data quality, accelerate new assortment introduction, and help the business respond more quickly to product and market updates.
- Communicate progress, risks, dependencies, scope decisions, and trade-offs clearly across US and India Product, Engineering, and business teams.

Why you will love working at Williams-Sonoma, Inc.
- We're a successful, fast-growing company with an entrepreneurial vibe.
- A technologically and data-driven business.
- Competitive salaries and comprehensive health benefits.
- We're at the forefront of tech and retail, redefining technology for the next generation.
- We're passionate about our internal and external clients and live and breathe the client experience.
- We get to be creative on a daily basis.
- A smart, experienced leadership team that wants to do it right and is open to new ideas.
- We believe in autonomy and reward taking initiative.

We're excited about you because...
- You have 5+ years of Product Management, Technical Product Management, or senior business systems experience delivering technology solutions.
- You have experience delivering complex enterprise platforms, internal business tools, or multi-system programs with significant workflow and integration complexity, in close partnership with Engineering.
- You can translate business problems and workflows into detailed product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and scalable technology solutions.
- You can balance business workflow and change-management responsibilities with abstract technical concepts, complex platform architecture, attribution and data models, integrations, and system behavior.
- You have experience working with business operations users and driving change for enterprise tools or processes through stakeholder engagement, demonstrations, training, UAT, rollout support, and adoption.
- You bring strong analytical and problem-solving skills and can identify edge cases, evaluate trade-offs, and make decisions in ambiguous situations.
- You communicate clearly and operate effectively across geographically distributed Product, Engineering, business, and leadership teams.
- You hold a bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or have equivalent professional experience.
- You can work from our India Technology Center in Pune according to WSI's onsite and hybrid working requirements.

Technical Competencies Required
- Strong technical aptitude and the ability to engage meaningfully with engineers and architects on integrations, data models, system workflows, platform architecture, and technical trade-offs.
- Ability to create clear product artifacts, including requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, prioritized backlogs, and delivery plans.
- Understanding of enterprise platform integrations and upstream and downstream dependencies across product information, digital asset, content, image, and eCommerce systems.
- Experience defining UAT scenarios, coordinating business validation, triaging issues, and converting findings into actionable product improvements.
- Ability to define and track product success measures such as adoption, workflow efficiency, time to market, data quality, platform performance, and user satisfaction.

Preferred Experience
- Knowledge of retail, eCommerce, merchandising, product information, content management, or digital asset management.
- Experience with platforms such as PLM, PIM, DAM, CMS/WCM, WAM, vendor portals, or merchandising systems.
- Experience supporting enterprise platform modernization, legacy-system replacement, or multi-year transformation programs.

Why Join Williams-Sonoma India Technology Center
- Our people-first and performance-driven culture means that we provide opportunities to grow and build a career, and invest in the well-being of our associates, including comprehensive benefits to support you and your family.
- Scale and innovation of a Fortune 500 company combined with a high-ownership environment that empowers associates to make real impact.
- Build and shape large-scale digital commerce and merchandising platforms serving millions of customers worldwide, working on systems that run at global scale.
- Continuous learning environment with opportunities to work on cutting-edge technologies, AI-driven solutions, and large-scale technology challenges.
- Hybrid work model designed for flexibility and collaboration, with two in-office days for team engagement.

jobs.title: Tech Principal Product Manager - Inventory Managment
jobs.description:
About the Team
You will be a key member of the Supply Chain Product Management team responsible for improving how Williams-Sonoma, Inc. plans, forecasts, allocates, replenishes, and manages inventory across brands, channels, categories, and fulfillment nodes. The team partners closely with Merchandising, Inventory Management, Planning, Allocation, Replenishment, Supply Chain, Stores, eCommerce, Finance, Analytics, and Technology to deliver scalable product capabilities that improve business planning, inventory productivity, forecast accuracy, in-stock performance, operational efficiency, and customer experience.

About the Role
Williams-Sonoma, Inc. is in the business of enhancing the quality of our customers’ lives at home. This Principal Product Manager role will be focused on driving product strategy and execution across core inventory management and planning capabilities, including Merch Financial Planning, Demand Forecasting, Assortment Planning, Allocation, Replenishment, and Inventory Optimization.
This role will help define and deliver capabilities that improve how the business plans demand, builds assortments, manages inventory investments, allocates product, replenishes inventory, and responds to changing customer, channel, and supply chain conditions. The right candidate will bring deep retail planning and inventory management experience, strong product management discipline, and the ability to translate complex business processes into scalable technology-enabled products and capabilities.
This role requires a product leader who can operate across strategy and execution: framing business opportunities, shaping roadmaps, aligning stakeholders, defining product requirements, evaluating solution alternatives, partnering with engineering and analytics teams, and ensuring delivered capabilities create measurable business value. Product strategy should start with the business problem, desired outcomes, and required capabilities rather than a predetermined technology solution.

Responsibilities
- Own the product lifecycle for inventory management from ideation through adoption, continuously measuring business outcomes, incorporating customer and stakeholder feedback, and evolving the product roadmap to maximize business value.
- Drive the adoption of AI, machine learning, automation, and decision-support capabilities to improve planning quality, accelerate product delivery, reduce manual effort, and enable smarter business decision making. Partner with Analytics and Engineering teams to identify, prioritize, and deliver high-value AI use cases across the Inventory Management domain.
- Leverage generative AI and modern product management tools to improve product discovery, requirements development, backlog quality, documentation, and team productivity while championing responsible AI adoption across the product domain.
- Lead end-to-end product discovery by partnering with business stakeholders to define strategy, prioritize opportunities, and translate business needs into product roadmaps, epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes.
- Partner with Engineering, Architecture, Analytics, and Program Management to execute product roadmaps, manage tradeoffs and dependencies, and deliver high-quality capabilities through Agile delivery.
- Lead product strategy across demand forecasting, assortment planning, merch financial planning, allocation, replenishment, and inventory optimization to improve forecast accuracy, inventory productivity, service levels, and financial performance.
- Advance merch financial planning capabilities that improve visibility into inventory investments, sales, margin, receipts, turn, open-to-buy, and related financial planning metrics.
- Drive allocation and replenishment capabilities that improve product placement, inventory availability, inventory productivity, sell-through, and customer fulfillment outcomes.
- Identify and prioritize opportunities to reduce manual work, spreadsheet dependency, process fragmentation, and operational friction across planning and inventory workflows.
- Partner with Analytics and Technology teams to deliver advanced forecasting, optimization, decision-support, and automation capabilities through the most appropriate combination of internally developed products, commercial Inventory Management packaged solutions, platform extensions, data products, and other technology approaches.
- Define product success metrics and measurement plans tied to forecast accuracy, in-stock performance, inventory productivity, sell-through, margin, planning cycle time, adoption, exception reduction, and operational efficiency.
- Provide clear recommendations on roadmap priorities, sequencing, tradeoffs, dependencies, risks, solution alternatives, and value realization to business partners and senior Technology leadership.
- Support organizational change management for new planning and inventory capabilities, including stakeholder alignment, process documentation, training, UAT, readiness, hyper-care, and adoption tracking.
- Establish and maintain strong product management practices and documentation across Jira, Confluence, and related product management tools to improve backlog quality, transparency, knowledge sharing, and team productivity.
- Ensure product capabilities are designed with appropriate controls, data quality, role-based access, audit considerations, and operational governance.
- Remain current with retail, supply chain, planning, forecasting, allocation, replenishment, AI, and inventory optimization trends, and apply relevant external practices to WSI’s product strategy.

Criteria
- 10+ years of related experience in Product Management, Inventory Management, Merch Financial Planning, Demand Forecasting, Assortment Planning, Allocation, Replenishment, Supply Chain, retail technology, or a related techno-functional discipline, with demonstrated experience delivering enterprise-scale planning, inventory, merchandising, or supply chain capabilities.
- Deep understanding of retail planning and inventory management, including financial planning, demand forecasting, assortment planning, allocation, replenishment, inventory optimization, and exception management.
- Strong product management discipline, with demonstrated ability to translate complex business processes and customer needs into product strategy, roadmaps, requirements, epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes; experience using Jira, Confluence, or similar product management tools.
- Strong analytical and business orientation, with the ability to use data, business metrics, financial impact, and operational performance to shape product decisions, prioritize investments, and measure value realization.
- Experience applying AI, machine learning, automation, optimization, or advanced analytics to improve planning, product management, operational efficiency, or customer outcomes, with the ability to identify and prioritize high-value AI-enabled capabilities.
- Demonstrated experience modernizing fragmented or manual planning processes into scalable, governed, system-enabled capabilities, including the ability to evaluate build, buy, extend, partner, and retirement options based on business value, architecture, risk, cost, and speed to value.
- Strong cross-functional leadership and influence, with the ability to partner effectively with senior business, Analytics, Engineering, Architecture, and Program Management stakeholders, lead through ambiguity, manage tradeoffs and dependencies, and drive alignment across a matrixed organization.
- Experience in large-scale, multi-channel or omnichannel retail environments strongly preferred, including experience with internally developed products, commercial Inventory Management packaged solutions, or hybrid technology approaches. Relevant retail planning consulting experience is also desirable.
- Strong communication and delivery discipline, with experience across Agile, Scrum, Lean, and/or waterfall delivery models and the ability to clearly communicate product strategy, priorities, risks, tradeoffs, and business outcomes to stakeholders at all levels.
- Bachelor’s degree or more in Supply Chain, Business, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Analytics, or a related field or equivalent work experience.
- This role requires being onsite in the San Francisco CA office Monday through Thursday.
- Some travel may be required to WSI corporate, store, distribution, care center, manufacturing, or supply chain locations within the United States.

Our Culture & Values
We believe that taking care of our people is vital to our success and we strive to offer equitable and transparent practices for all. We prioritize connection, growth, and wellbeing.
People First
Putting People First means investing in overall well-being and opportunities to grow and advance within the organization. Depending on the position and location, here are a few highlights of what benefits may be available:
Benefits
- A generous discount on all WSI brands
- A 401(k) plan and other investment opportunities
- Paid vacations, holidays, and time off to volunteer
- Health benefits, dental and vision insurance, including same-sex domestic partner benefits
- Tax-free commuter benefits
- A wellness program that supports your physical, financial and emotional health

Continued Learning
- In-person and online learning opportunities through WSI University
- Cross-brand and cross-function career opportunities
- Resources for self-development
- Advisor (Mentor) program
- Career development workshops, learning programs, and speaker series

jobs.title: Assistant, Digital Product Operations - Pottery Barn Teen
jobs.description:
About the Team
The Digital Product Operations team plays a critical role in shaping the digital customer experience across Pottery Barn Kids, PB Teen and Dormify bringing our brand vision to life through the management of the product page. Our team owns the strategy, execution, analysis and maintenance of the product experience across all three brands. This includes product page management, systems testing, site improvements and optimization efforts that support a stronger customer experience. We partner closely with cross-functional teams across Merchandising, eCommerce, Creative, Technology and Operations to deliver accurate, inspiring and scalable online experiences that support the customer through the purchase journey.

About the Role
This is an opportunity to help shape the digital customer experience for a highly visible and commercially important category. You will work with creative and collaborative partners to deliver inspiring product pages that support customer discovery, category growth, and brand storytelling.

We are seeking a customer-obsessed, analytical, detail-oriented, and collaborative Assistant of Digital Product Operations to assist in day-to-day digital merchandising operations for our furniture category across Pottery Barn Kids, Pottery Barn Teen, and Dormify. This role supports strategy, execution, analysis, and maintenance of the product page, the most valuable page within our site, for this category across the three brands.

The Assistant serves as a champion of the customer experience on the product page, focusing equally on inspiration and information to drive conversion and revenue. This role assists the basket-building strategy, structural playbook, testing, and performance metrics of the product page. The Assistant uses data, customer behavior, and cross-functional input to identify opportunities, reduce friction, and continuously improve the digital experience. Additionally, this role owns all activities within our WCM platform including site builds and technology enhancements.

This role partners closely with Site Merchandising, Merchandising, Creative, UX/Product, Analytics, Technology, and Operations teams to deliver seasonal launches, category optimization, maintenance, and new tech functionality on time and with accuracy.

Responsibilities
Category Execution
- Manage the SKU creation and generation of product pages within the designated category for seasonal launches. Own testing in partnership with Site Merchandising and Creative for accuracy. Ensure on-time launch delivery based on careful calendar planning, workflow management, and prioritization.

- Maintain the product page playbook for your category including basket-building, image/video strategy, structure, and UX/UI across desktop, mobile, and app. Ensure adherence to the playbook. Partner with Site Merchandising and Creative on changes.

- Maintain awareness of customer needs, category trends, competitive activity, business performance, and eCommerce best practices to inform recommendations and execution.

Analytics & Performance Management
- Assist in weekly product page performance reporting for your category using analytics and data. Clearly communicate to cross functional stakeholders with insights and actions.

- Monitor key product page metrics, including traffic, conversion funnel, product finding behavior, basket building, product recommendations, channel performance, and promotional performance.

- Develop recaps and actionable recommendations to the Manager, escalating risks and opportunities as needed.

Customer Experience & Optimization
- Champion the customer product page experience and drive optimizations that reduce friction and make the shopping journey more intuitive and inspiring. Execute strategies to weave storytelling and brand building moments into the purchase journey without adding friction.

- Participate in weekly site testing. Triage ad hoc issues and perform maintenance updates.

- Partner with UX/Product and Technology to launch new functionality, tools, and workflows.

- Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership

- Contribute to a collaborative, accountable team environment focused on customer-first execution, accuracy, agility, and continuous improvement.

- Build strong working relationships with Merchandising, Site Merchandising, Creative, Analytics, Technology, and Operations partners to ensure alignment and flawless execution.

Criteria
- 1-2 years of eCommerce merchandising or operations experience required.
- BA/BS degree required.
- Advanced Excel skills required; strong PowerPoint and business recap skills preferred.
- Basic web analytics experience required; experience using Adobe Analytics highly preferred.
- Experience using web content management, eCommerce, or site merchandising systems preferred.
- Basic understanding of site merchandising, customer journey optimization, product discovery, promotions, and digital storytelling.
- Excellent communication, collaboration, organization, and project management skills.
- Comfort with AI and desire to continually search for workflow efficiency and optimization.
- Customer-first and passionate about eCommerce, product discovery, and evolving consumer behavior.
- Highly detail-oriented while able to connect day-to-day execution to broader category and customer experience goals.
- Collaborative, agile, and committed to building positive cross functional relationships.
- A practical problem solver who identifies opportunities, removes roadblocks, and drives continuous improvement.
- Good communicator and willing to share a point of view.
- This role requires being onsite in the San Francisco office Monday through Thursday and Friday as optional in the office
